<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
For every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^2$ and every $t>0$, with $f_t=\mu*\gamma_t$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{I(t)I''(t)\geq\frac{231691}{250000}[I'(t)]^2.}
 \label{eq:lowerthm}
\end{equation}
No symmetry, log-concavity, finite-variance, or finite-entropy assumption on $\mu$ is required.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Equation \eqref{eq:divided}, positivity of $H$, and positivity of the Gram matrices give \eqref{eq:tauineq}. The positive-time Gaussian estimates justify the cutoff limit \eqref{eq:divzero}. The quadratic in $\tau$ is minimized at $\tau=Q/I>0$, yielding $D\geq c_0Q^2/I$. Finally use $Q=-I'$ and $D=I''$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
